theAdmissionBoundary.v2Defect: B-C2V2-01, critical. v2's InvocationPlan covered snapshot capture AND allocated ExecutionId, and declared that ANY failure at that level is pre-admission and never a Run verdict. But D9's analysis-snapshot-invalidated golden carries admission=admitted, lifecycle=coherent-terminal-run, a RunId, committed durability, and class=indeterminate. The same snapshot failure had incompatible identity and termination semantics depending on which artifact you read.
theAdmissionBoundary.resolution: The boundary is not invocation-vs-execution. It is REQUEST VALIDATION vs ATTEMPT ADMISSION, and snapshot capture sits AFTER admission.

levels.onFailure: request-rejected, or operational-failed if the host itself faulted. No ExecutionId, no AttemptRecord, no Run. This is the ONLY pre-admission level.
operational-failed. An AttemptRecord exists from this point.
levels.why: ExecutionId is an ATTEMPT anchor (EC-6) and must exist before any work that can fail in an interesting way, or a crash cannot name the orphan.

levels.onFailure: POST-ADMISSION. Convergence exhaustion seals a coherent terminal Run reporting indeterminate with Coverage naming the cause. It is NOT a rejected request.
per stage semantics; the Run is sealed either way

attemptRecord.what: The durable record that an attempt was admitted, keyed by ExecutionId, existing before any Run is sealed.
attemptRecord.why: It is what makes 'every analysis attempt gets an identity and is recorded by default' true, and what lets orphan recovery name a specific abandoned attempt rather than inferring one.
attemptRecord.relationToRun: An AttemptRecord may seal into exactly one Run, or be abandoned. It is never itself a Run and carries no verdict.

theAdmissionBoundary.checkedAgainstD9: C1X asserts that every D9 golden's admission axis is consistent with the level its scenario belongs to, read from the LIVE D9 artifact.

planIntent.purpose: The closed, fully resolved request representation on which product and capability admission is decided BEFORE ExecutionId or AttemptRecord allocation. It makes every authority-bearing choice visible while rejection is still a D9 pre-run request rejection.

lifecycle.createdAt: request-validation, after project/configuration/contribution/capability resolution and before attempt-admission
lifecycle.onInvalidOrExcluded: Reject at request-validation. No ExecutionId, AttemptRecord, SnapshotId, PlanId or Run exists.
lifecycle.onValidatedStoredRead: For intentKind=stored-view, freeze and commit the exact StoredViewIntent and copy it into a RequestId-owned PreparedStoredRead. No ExecutionId, AttemptRecord, SnapshotId, PlanId, ExecutionPlan or Run is created.
lifecycle.onAdmittedAnalysis: For intentKind=analysis, freeze the exact PlanIntent, compute planIntentCommitment, then atomically store admittedPlanIntent, admissionDescriptor and the commitment in the newly allocated AttemptRecord at attempt-admission.
lifecycle.immutability: The admitted PlanIntent is immutable. Snapshot binding may add SnapshotId and derive PlanId; it may not add, remove, default or substitute an authority-bearing intent field.

validationTotality.domain: Every successfully parsed JSON value at EVERY position of the request: the root, every object key and every array index at unlimited depth, CONTAINER AND SCALAR LEAF alike, carrying any JSON type.
validationTotality.result: Exactly Valid(typed PlanIntent) or Invalid(non-empty typed C2I finding list). Validation never raises a language or runtime exception for caller-controlled parsed JSON.
validationTotality.boundary: Invalid returns during request-validation before ExecutionId, AttemptRecord, SnapshotId, PlanId, ExecutionPlan or Run allocation.
validationTotality.admitThenCommitClosure: NEW IN v4, and the half of the totality claim v3 did not make. Any PlanIntent the validator ADMITS must also ENCODE: canonical_plan_intent and plan_intent_commitment carry the same named-finding boundary the validator carries, so no value the validator admits can raise at the encoder. v3 admitted schemaVersion 1.0 and then raised an unguarded ValueError inside the encoder, which is where the defect reached the evaluation-proof authority join.
validationTotality.measurementRule: A totality claim is only as wide as the instrument that measured it. v3's retained hostile corpus was PINNED to exactly four collection-adjacent scalars by four hostile types and could therefore never inject at a top-level or descriptor-level scalar leaf, which is precisely where LB-C2-01 lived. v4's generator enumerates every position INCLUDING scalar leaves and publishes the live measured counts in hostileScalarLeafTotality; the checker recomputes them on every run and treats a shortfall as a finding, not an omission.

canonicalIdentifier.normalization: ASCII subset and therefore NFC; alternate case, empty components and surrounding whitespace reject.

runId.scope: C-2 stored-read wire address; derivation/custody remains a Run identity concern

canonicalRelativePath.rule: NFC UTF-8, forward slash separators, no empty/dot/dot-dot segment, no leading slash, backslash, NUL or drive prefix.

boundedParameterValue.maps: Keys are unique canonicalIdentifier values sorted by UTF-8 bytes; unknown contribution-specific keys are rejected by that contribution's already-verified schema.
boundedParameterValue.arrays: Order is preserved unless the owning field declares set semantics.
boundedParameterValue.forbidden: floating point, byte strings, non-NFC strings, values outside signed 64-bit range

schemaVersionInteger.rule: The JSON value MUST be an integer. A JSON boolean is NOT an integer, even though a naive host comparison makes true equal 1. A JSON number carrying a fractional part is NOT an integer, even though a naive host comparison makes 1.0 equal 1. Both spellings are REJECTED during request-validation, before any ExecutionId, AttemptRecord, SnapshotId, PlanId or ExecutionPlan exists.
schemaVersionInteger.v3Defect: LB-C2-01. v3's checker guarded both schemaVersion fields with a bare inequality against the integer 1. A wire PlanIntent spelling schemaVersion as true was ADMITTED and then committed to a SECOND, different digest, so the closed schema had two admissible type-distinct spellings of its own version field, each minting its own PlanId. A wire PlanIntent spelling it as 1.0 was ADMITTED and then raised an unguarded ValueError inside the canonical encoder, which validate_plan_intent's totality boundary did not cover. 20 cases: 7 valid fixtures, both intentKind branches, both schemaVersion positions.

planId.join: BYTE-EXACT. check-c2-v4.py compares this pattern to the live resolved-inputs.v2.json value and fails on any drift, exactly as C2I-OP does for REQUEST-ID-V1.
planId.ownership: The GRAMMAR and the DERIVATION are owned by RESOLVED-INPUTS and validated by check-resolved-inputs.py. What C-2 owns, and what v3 failed to bind, is the VALUE its own ExecutionPlan envelope carries.

snapshotId.ownership: Grammar and derivation owned by RESOLVED-INPUTS.

executionId.ownershipHonesty: NO cross-contract EXECUTION-ID-V1 owner exists in this corpus. Unlike planId and snapshotId, this grammar cannot be joined byte-exactly to another artifact, so C-2 declares it here and takes ownership. The spelling follows the only canonical ExecutionId text in the corpus, resolved-inputs.v2.json#planIdContract.goldenVectors.negative[2].addTopLevel.executionId, and the same host-minted 128-bit shape as REQUEST-ID-V1. If an owning artifact later declares EXECUTION-ID-V1, this declaration must become a byte-exact join and C-2 must yield ownership. Recorded as residual RES-C2V4-01.

subjectScopeCommitment.deferred: COMPUTATION and VERIFICATION remain owned by the retention/evidence surface (R1-C2-03, adjudicated RESOLVED). v4 does not reopen that deferral and does not claim to verify what a subject scope contains.
subjectScopeCommitment.v3Defect: LB-C2-03. v3 bound this field by KEY PRESENCE alone. Every JSON value was conformant, including null, and the value all three valid coverage fixtures actually shipped, the literal string "sha256:...", violated C-2's own sha256Id grammar. A Coverage entry with subjectScopeCommitment null satisfied v3, which is the precise negation of the property the field exists to create. Deferring HOW a commitment is computed never required leaving its WIRE TYPE unconstrained.

contribution.ordering: Strict ascending byte order by activationId; activationId is unique. Ordering is rejected rather than silently repaired before commitment.

budgets.shape: closed string-keyed map from canonical unit-bearing budget IDs to integer values 1..9223372036854775807
budgets.ordering: keys unique; canonical JSON sorts them by Unicode scalar value

target.resolutionRule: Resolve RunId during request-validation and require the stored sealed-manifest bytes to match sealedManifestDigest before reading any projection or artifact.

encoding.name: opensip-canonical-json-v1
encoding.dataModel: JSON objects, arrays, strings, booleans, signed integers and null only; floating-point numbers are forbidden.
encoding.objects: Duplicate keys are rejected by the parser. Keys are NFC strings and are emitted in ascending Unicode scalar-value order with no insignificant whitespace.
encoding.strings: NFC before encoding; UTF-8 without BOM; JSON escapes are lowercase, shortest required escapes; solidus is not escaped.
encoding.integers: Shortest base-10 form; no leading plus or leading zero except zero itself.
encoding.closure: The PlanIntent schema is closed before encoding, so an unknown field cannot hide outside the commitment.

canonicalCommitment.planIdentityJoin: The canonical PlanId preimage MUST contain this exact planIntentCommitment as a typed field; PlanId validation recomputes it from the frozen admitted PlanIntent.
canonicalCommitment.totalityBoundary: canonical_plan_intent rejects floating-point values, non-string object keys and keys that collide after NFC normalisation. In v4 those rejections are reachable ONLY for values the validator already rejected: the validator's declared-integer guards run first, so the admit-then-raise path LB-C2-01 exercised does not exist. The property is measured, not asserted: every enumerated hostile injection that the validator admits is then encoded, and any admit-then-raise is a named finding.

attemptAndExecutionJoin.appliesWhen: intentKind=analysis. intentKind=stored-view creates neither an attempt nor an ExecutionPlan.
attemptAndExecutionJoin.attemptRecordRule: At the same transaction that allocates ExecutionId, store the full frozen admittedPlanIntent, its exact AnalysisIntentV1.admissionDescriptor and planIntentCommitment. The descriptor field equals the subobject byte-for-byte; omission or difference is invalid and no snapshot work may start.
attemptAndExecutionJoin.equalityRule: Before cache lookup, provider dispatch or stage execution: recompute the commitment from AttemptRecord.admittedPlanIntent; require exact equality with AttemptRecord.planIntentCommitment, ExecutionPlan.planIntentCommitment and planIdentityInputs.planIntentCommitment. Require AttemptRecord.admissionDescriptor equal the admitted subobject. Require planIdentityInputs fields 3..8 and 10..12 equal the mapped AdmissionDescriptorV1 fields, ExecutionPlan.projectId equal descriptor.scope.projectId, and ExecutionPlan.stages equal descriptor.workflow.stages. No field is compared by partial identity pairs.
attemptAndExecutionJoin.postAdmissionFields: planIdentityInputs.snapshotId is the sealed SnapshotId, planSchemaMajor is integer constant 1, and semanticUniverses is the closed provider-universe array derived under the admitted provider contributions. These are the only PlanDescriptor fields constructed after attempt admission; they cannot alter the admitted descriptor.
attemptAndExecutionJoin.substitutionRule: Recomputing a commitment for a changed intent does not re-admit it: the changed value still mismatches the immutable AttemptRecord commitment. A new intent requires a new request-validation and a new attempt.

identifierWireTypes.v3Defect: LB-C2-05. v3 named planId, snapshotId and executionId, declared no wire type for any of them, shipped the noncanonical placeholders plan-1, snap-1 and exec-1 in both the contract and the checker, and accepted null, string, integer, boolean, float, list and object at executionPlan.planId and attemptRecord.executionId without a finding. That is the same defect class already repaired for RequestId (C2I-OP) and ProjectId (C2I-TM); the repair standard was applied inconsistently inside one contract.

requestIdContract.authority: host-minted-reserved at first trusted ingress before parsing or stored-state lookup; public callers MUST NOT supply, replace or reuse it
requestIdContract.semanticExclusion: RequestId remains contextual and is forbidden from PlanIntent, planIntentCommitment, SnapshotId, PlanId, EvidenceDigest and Run identity.

storedViewJoin.equalityRule: Before storage access, recompute planIntentCommitment from RequestContext.admittedPlanIntent and require PreparedStoredRead requestId/commitment and every StoredViewIntent field to be exactly equal. A changed RunId, manifest digest, query, result or retention selector requires a new RequestId request-validation; it cannot ride the old commitment.
storedViewJoin.identityRule: The same canonical host-minted-reserved REQUEST-ID-V1 is mandatory in both envelopes and is the only newly allocated lifecycle/correlation identity. Malformed, non-string, caller-supplied or unequal RequestId rejects before storage access. The selected existing RunId may appear in events, but there is no new ExecutionId, AttemptRecord, SnapshotId, PlanId, ExecutionPlan or Run.
storedViewJoin.materialisationRule: The operation reads only already-sealed state. A missing artifact/fact relation/retention state returns typed unavailable and does not trigger analysis or provider startup.

Representation is not runtime authority and does not discharge ARCH.PROBE-CONTRACT. The v1 overlay must be total over these enums but is owned by DELIVERY.

integerConstantFields.why: LB-C2-01 was not one typo. It was a CLASS: a bare equality test against an integer literal applied to a value that came off the wire. This section enumerates every such field so the checker can enforce the class mechanically instead of one site at a time, and so a fifth site cannot be added silently.
integerConstantFields.rule: Every field below is validated by exact TYPE first and value second: the value must be a JSON integer, must not be a JSON boolean, and must not be a JSON number with a fractional part. check-c2-v4.py additionally scans its own abstract syntax tree and refuses to report clean if any reachable validator compares a wire-sourced value to a numeric literal outside the declared guard helpers.

effectTaxonomy.v2Defect: B-C2V2-03 and A1-C2V2-02. PS-12 said effectful work is representable ONLY as a Probe. Semantic providers and external scanners read snapshot subsets, spawn compiler and toolchain processes, write ephemeral output, and under grant reach the network. Every one of them is effectful and none is a Probe. A valid scanner therefore either violated PS-12 or had to be mislabelled a Probe, which would erase its distinct Coverage and failure semantics.
effectTaxonomy.resolution: Three classes, distinguished by WHAT is affected, not by whether a side effect occurs at all.

classes.affects: the project or the external world, as the SUBJECT of observation
classes.rule: Only a probe stage. This is what v2 was actually trying to say.

classes.affects: the host's own scratch space and child processes, never the project's meaning
examples: spawning a compiler or language server
network access under an explicit grant
classes.rule: Permitted for a DECLARED operator (semantic provider, external scanner) under a typed capability grant, host-supervised. Not a probe. Retains its own Coverage and failure semantics.
Rule and policy evaluation are pure over facts and hold NO effect authority of any kind. This is the prohibition that survives review.

effectTaxonomy.whatCCannotClose: The MECHANISM that denies a mislabelled stage its authority does not exist. ARCH.PROBE-CONTRACT is REOPENED precisely because interface labels do not confine linked TCB code. C-2 declares the requirement and DEPENDS on that mechanism; it does not discharge it. See dischargeStatus.

admissionMode.v2Defect: B-C2V2-04 and A1-C2V2-06. v2 tied createsRun to the RESULT NOUN — fact query false, rule findings true, reduction candidates true. Run creation then became a property of what you asked to see rather than of whether new authoritative analysis was admitted. Stored findings can be read without analysis; a fact query can explicitly admit missing derivation.
admissionMode.resolution: Run creation is a function of the closed PlanIntent intentKind and nothing else. The result noun is orthogonal; admissionMode is retained only as this historical decision heading, not as a wire field.

modes.rule: Answers only from already-materialised facts and already-sealed Runs. If a required relation is absent, returns a typed unavailable response naming the missing requirement. NEVER materialises.
Explicitly admitted. May materialise required facts. Seals a Run.

admissionMode.orthogonality: Every result noun is reachable in BOTH modes. Reduction candidates read from a sealed Run create no Run; reduction that must materialise facts requires analysis admission. That is the split A1-C2V2-06 asked for, generalised.

coverageKey.v2Defect: B-C2V2-05. The key carried one languageOrSemanticUniverseId and an opaque subjectScopePartition. Relations like imports, calls and package cycles cross universes, so complete SOURCE-side extraction could be mistaken for complete TARGET resolution, and two implementations could partition exact Coverage differently.

key.typeRule: The registry lookup is driven by TYPE, never by truthiness. v3 wrote `if factplane and relation:` and therefore SKIPPED the declared C2X registry check for all six falsy JSON values - null, 0, false, the empty string, the empty array and the empty object - so a Coverage entry naming no relation at all was C-2-conformant (LB-C2-02). A non-string relation is now a C2X finding.

key.constraint: must be a rung of THAT relation's ladder
the semantic universe of the subject
the semantic universe of the object; equals sourceUniverseId for intra-universe relations; REQUIRED and possibly different for cross-universe relations
key.why: this is the field whose absence let source-complete read as target-complete

key.constraint: an explicit set commitment over the subjects examined, not an opaque partition label
key.why: makes both membership and NON-membership checkable, so 'we found nothing' is distinguishable from 'we looked at nothing'
key.boundHere: SHAPE ONLY; computation and verification stay deferred (R1-C2-03).

key.constraint: same source bytes under a different producer is a different fact

consumerStatus.rule: Every rule and query records its status against the EXACT Coverage entries it consumed, never against a Plan-level summary.

coverageKey.languageTierLink: A syntax-tier language produces unavailable entries for its resolved rungs with deficiency language-tier-unsupported — the mechanism that makes the P-4 loud-tier decision observable rather than editorial.

conditionallyRequired.targetUniverseId: REQUIRED when relation is one of crossUniverseRelations

entrySchema.rootRule: A Coverage entry that is not a non-empty JSON object is REJECTED with the named finding C2X-ROOT. v3's validate_coverage RAISED on seven hostile roots - null, 0, true, 1.5, a string, an empty array and a non-empty array (LB-C2-02). The public validator is now total: hostile parsed JSON at every node returns findings, never a traceback.
entrySchema.totalityRule: validate_coverage carries the same named-finding boundary that validate_plan_intent and check() carry, so a missed wrong-type traversal becomes a deterministic C2X finding rather than a host fault.
entrySchema.v3Measurement: 81 hostile node-by-type mutations of the intra-universe-complete entry produced 9 exceptions and 58 zero-finding results: 58 of 81 mutations produced no finding at all.

subjectScopeCommitmentExamples.rule: Every valid coverage fixture's subjectScopeCommitment is SHA-256 over the exact UTF-8 preimage declared beside it, so a reviewer can verify that the shape binding is satisfied by a reproducible digest and not by an opaque constant. This is an EXAMPLE ENCODING for the fixtures only. It is NOT a claim about how a product computes a real subject-scope commitment; that remains owned by the retention/evidence surface.

executionPlan.custody: public contract; may be selected by a data-only profile
executionPlan.boundTo: exactly one frozen admitted PlanIntent, one SnapshotId and one PlanId
executionPlan.intentBinding: planIntent.attemptAndExecutionJoin is normative. The stage-only planFixtures below exercise the logical stage schema; intentBindingFixtures exercise complete ExecutionPlan envelopes and the pre-/post-admission equality rule.
executionPlan.exhaustiveness: Closed. An unknown kind is REJECTED, not ignored. A fifth public kind is a Plan schema major.

stageSchemas.why: B-C2V2-06 and A1-C2V2-07: PS-01/02/11 all depend on a serialised schema with closed enums and private-field rejection, and none existed. Without this the binding object could not distinguish a conforming Plan from one carrying private operators.

fact-derivation.note: external-scanner is where trivy/gitleaks-class work lives (A1-C2V2-04). It is a declared fact-derivation operator with its own authority value, its own Coverage entries and its own failure semantics — not a probe, and not a rule.

rule-evaluation.note: The forbidden list is the schema-level form of the prohibition. It is necessary and NOT sufficient — schema rejection is not runtime denial.

privateOperators.rule: MUST NOT appear in a serialised ExecutionPlan.
privateOperators.plannerFreedom: Insert, reorder, fuse or elide freely, provided the logical stage contract and the resulting EvidenceDigest are unchanged under identical exact Coverage.

requiredness.rule: Every rule in a Plan is REQUIRED or OPTIONAL, declared, never defaulted silently.
requiredness.requiredFault: A fault or budget exhaustion in a REQUIRED rule becomes a Coverage entry and forces policy indeterminate.
requiredness.optionalFault: Isolated, recorded as a diagnostic and a Coverage entry; does not force indeterminate.
requiredness.whyThisWasABlocker: v1 said 'rule fault is isolated and does not fail the plan.' Applied to a required rule, that permits a passing verdict from an analysis that did not run — the exact false pass the sealed invariant forbids.

hostileScalarLeafTotality.why: The dominant failure mode in this corpus is a totality or coverage claim quantified over a region the instrument could not observe. Five surfaces have now shipped one. hostileScalarLeafTotality.enumeration: The root, every object key and every array index at unlimited depth, CONTAINER AND SCALAR LEAF alike. Every enumerated path is round-trip verified before it is counted: a path that does not resolve back to the node it names is excluded and counted separately.
hostileScalarLeafTotality.unknownKeyInjection: At every enumerated object position an unknown key is also injected, so record closure is measured at the same resolution as type totality.

contractRoot.what: every position of this contract document itself, driven through check(), the CLI boundary
contractRoot.executedLayers: every check() layer except the leaf-inclusive census layer, which is itself the instrument and is executed in full over the fixture surfaces on every ordinary invocation. Re-running the instrument inside each of ~23000 whole-document mutations would multiply the cost by two orders of magnitude. The path census below is recomputed and compared on EVERY invocation, so a change to the space the selftest measured is detected even when the execution matrix has not run.
contractRoot.guardedEscapesRule: MUST be zero. check() is the CLI boundary and the property it declares is that hostile parsed JSON becomes a named C2-TOTALITY-* finding, never a traceback.
contractRoot.unguardedEscapesRule: Reported, NOT required to be zero, and the number is published in the --selftest report rather than pinned here because pinning a count of the document's own mutations inside that document has no fixed point. The distinction is deliberate and is the honest scope of the claim. A CONTRACT DOCUMENT is an authoring artifact, not caller-controlled input: the inner reader _check consumes it structurally and the named-finding boundary is the correct place to convert an authoring fault into a report. The WIRE REQUEST surfaces are different - they are caller-controlled, they are what LB-C2-01, LB-C2-02 and LB-C2-04 were about, and they are total UNGUARDED as well as guarded: 0 unguarded escapes across all three, published above and compared on every run. Stating this split is the point; a single number covering both would be the coverage claim over an unobserved region that this corpus keeps shipping.

hostileScalarLeafTotality.comparisonRule: check-c2-v4.py recomputes every number in this section on every run and compares it. Understating the space is a finding, not an omission. The mutation suite additionally NARROWS the generator back to container-only positions and requires the published counts to become detectably wrong, so the leaf-inclusive enumeration is proved load-bearing rather than declared.

exitCodes.1: findings in the candidate, or an escaped mutation in --selftest
exitCodes.2: unsupported invocation, unreadable candidate, or a pinned input that does not hash to its declared digest
exitCodes.3: --selftest REFUSED because the base candidate is not clean. A mutation suite over a dirty base is not an oracle: every row echoes the pre-existing failure and reports 'all rejected'. Exit 3 is distinct from green 0, from findings 1 and from bad invocation 2, and can never be absorbed into a pass.

checkerModeContract.hashBeforeExecution: Every pinned transitive input is read once, hash-verified against its declared digest, and then parsed or EXECUTED from that verified byte string rather than re-read from disk.
checkerModeContract.distinctOutputs: Normal mode and --selftest emit different reports with different line counts and different digests. A checker whose --selftest is byte-identical to its normal output has a dead selftest path.
checkerModeContract.authorityBoundary: A green run is checker-scope evidence authored by the same lane that authored this contract. It is NOT independent review, NOT qualification, NOT demonstration, NOT a seal and NOT product acceptance.

residuals.detail: Carried unchanged from the live-bytes review's RES-01, because repairing it would move a planIntentCommitment and v4's first obligation is that all seven vectors reproduce byte-exactly. Across all seven valid fixtures the committed data contains no non-ASCII key or string, no control character, no character requiring a JSON escape, no negative integer and no integer above 2^53. The NFC clause, the lowercase-shortest-escape clause, the ascending Unicode scalar-value key order clause and the no-leading-plus clause are therefore still untested by any retained vector. Two independent implementers agreeing 7/7 is weaker evidence than it appears. The right repair is an ADDITIONAL valid vector, which is a new commitment and belongs to a version that is not also carrying a REJECT repair.
